instruction.text: This is a map of Western South America. Select the lake to learn more.

hint.text: A navigable lake is a lake that is deep, wide and calm enough for ships and boats to travel on it safely.
hint.label: Navigable lake

atoms.b: Located on the border between Bolivia and Peru, Lake Titicaca is South America’s ((smallest ++largest)) lake, and the highest navigable lake in the world.
The lake was very ((useless ++important)) in Inca mythology as the local people believed its waters were the birthplace of their gods and the universe.
Today, it is inhabited by people of the indigenous Uros tribe, who have lived on the lake for hundreds of years on floating ((roads ++islands)) made entirely from dried grass.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Ecuador’s Galápagos Islands are a group of 20 volcanic islands located in the Pacific Ocean, 600 miles west of South America.
Around 97% of the Galápagos Islands is a designated national park, which strictly protects these natural areas from human activity and tourism.
The islands are home to many rare and unique animals such as giant tortoises, who can live for up to 150 years!
In 1835, Charles Darwin visited the islands and studied its wildlife, helping him to develop his theory of evolution.

atoms.b: Sitting at 2,430 m in the ((++mountains lakes)) of Peru, Machu Picchu was an ancient city built by the Inca Empire in the mid 1400s.
atoms.sound: Sitting at 2,430 m in the mountains of Peru, Mahchoo Peekchwoo was an ancient city built by the Inca Empire in the mid 1400s.

atoms.b: The city included houses, religious ((stores ++temples)) and many terraced farms, which were used to grow crops native to the ((++Americas Antarctic)), such as corn, potatoes and quinoa.

hint.text: Terraced farming is a popular method in many mountainous regions to maximise steep hillside space. Each terraced step collects rainwater, stops soil washing away and traps heat to help plants grow at high altitudes.
hint.label: Terraced farming

atoms.b: The ruins are one of the Seven Wonders of the World, and attract millions of ((birds ++tourists)) each year.

hint.label: Seven Wonders of the World
hint.text:
The Seven Wonders of the World are iconic historical landmarks:

• Great Wall of China (China)
• Petra (Jordan)
• The Colosseum (Italy)
• Chichen Itza (Mexico)
• Machu Picchu (Peru)
• Taj Mahal (India)
• Christ the Redeemer (Brazil)
hint.sound: The Seven Wonders of the World are iconic historical landmarks.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: At 5,500 miles long, the Andes are the longest mountain range in the world. They cross 7 countries along South America’s western coast, from near the Caribbean Sea to the southern tip of the continent.
Here you can find La Paz in Bolivia, which is the highest capital city in the world. Due to its unique, mountainous geography, the city is connected by the world’s longest urban cable car network.
Volcanic activity has also shaped the Andes for thousands of years, especially in Ecuador’s “Avenue of the Volcanoes”. Here you can find Cotopaxi, one of Earth’s highest active volcanoes.
atoms.sound: Volcanic activity has also shaped the Andes for thousands of years, especially in Ecuador’s “Avenue of the Volcanoes”. Here you can find Cotopaxi, one of Earth’s highest active volcanoes.

hint.sound: You can also find Ecuador’s tallest mountain here: Chimboarazo. While Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world by altitude, Chimboarazo is considered the tallest if you measure from the centre of the Earth! This is because the planet bulges around the Equator.
text: You can also find Ecuador’s tallest mountain here: Chimborazo. While Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world by altitude, Chimborazo is considered the tallest if you measure from the centre of the Earth! This is because the planet bulges around the Equator.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.text: Llamas and alpacas are native to the Andes and are perfectly adapted to the high altitudes. They are central to indigenous Andean culture and have provided meat, wool and transportation for centuries.
